Detailed Description of Action
200
The depletable nature and uncertain availability of most of the energy upon which the National relies for its economic and social well-being necessitates a national program for conserving energy. The gasoline shortages of the winter of 1973-1974 and the inflationary effect of rising fuel costs on almost all goods and services emphasize the need for conserving petroleum.
The significance of petroleum for this country is demonstrated by the fact that 46 percent of its annual energy needs are met by petroleum. Over half of the petroleum is used for transportation. In 1975, the figure was 55 percent. Highway transportation accounted for 46 percent of all petroleum consumed.
Title V requires the Administrator of the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration to establish average fuel economy standards (AFES's) for automobiles of not more than 6,000 pounds, gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR). The responsibility for implementing Title V was vested in the Secretary of Transportation and delegated to the Administrator (41 FR 25015, June 22, 1976).
